audit_note: 2026-10-16 independent re-verification: c8 pair re-run on fresh servers, acceptance re-measured at c8 and on natural text, spec=2 failure cause corrected. All numbers below are the verified values.

mtp_spec1.acceptance_note: 4.73% (c1) / 4.35% (c8) on random-token prompts; 16.64% on natural text (16 requests, temp=0). Even 16.6% is far below the 60-85% needed for MTP to pay off on this stack.

c8.verified: 2026-10-16 rerun; direction confirmed but value varies (554 vs 765 in two runs)

mtp_spec2.detail: Server crashes at model load: ValueError: Can't determine cudagraph shapes that are both a multiple of 3 (num_speculative_tokens + 1) required by spec-decode and 8 (tensor_parallel_size) required by sequence parallelism. NOT a quantization issue (Cline's earlier attribution was wrong). Fixable in principle via --disable-sequence-parallel, but pointless: acceptance is too low for spec=2 to help.

constraints.mtp_forces_eager: MTP on this stack requires enforce_eager=True; with eager=False the NPUModelRunner crashes at init (verified from 12:08 server log). So the ON-vs-OFF comparison includes the eager-vs-cudagraph penalty — it is the production-realistic comparison, not a pure MTP cost.
constraints.prompt_dependency: Acceptance depends strongly on prompt type: 4.4-4.7% (random tokens) vs 16.6% (natural text). Performance runs all used random tokens; relative ON-vs-OFF comparison remains fair since both arms used identical prompts.

c1.verdict: MTP=OFF slightly better (throughput +2.4%), TTFT negligible difference

c8.verdict: VERIFIED: MTP=ON cuts TTFT roughly in half at c8 (554 vs 1389 ms, direction stable across two runs) but loses 9-10% throughput/TPOT. Genuine trade-off, not noise.

c32.verdict: MTP=OFF better across all metrics at high concurrency

conclusion.rationale: Acceptance rate is 4.4-4.7% on synthetic and 16.6% on natural text — far too low for MTP to amortize its overhead (plus this stack forces eager mode with MTP). ON loses 2.4-10% throughput at every measured concurrency.
conclusion.c8_exception: At c=8 MTP=ON delivers ~2.5x lower TTFT (554 vs 1389 ms, verified) at the cost of ~9% throughput. If a deployment cares about first-token latency at moderate concurrency (c≈8) more than throughput, MTP=ON is a legitimate option. Treat the exact TTFT value with caution: two ON runs gave 554 and 765 ms.
conclusion.spec2_status: Unsupported as shipped (cudagraph shape conflict with TP=8 sequence parallelism); not worth enabling given low acceptance.
left_open: acceptance under production sampling (temp>0, real traffic distribution)
c8 TTFT mechanism: why MTP lowers prefill-visible TTFT — worth one vllm-ascend scheduler investigation if the c8 TTFT gain matters
